rubrics.justification: Description is largely consistent with a 3AB expanded blastocyst: thinning zona, strong ICM, and somewhat looser TE. It adds a few image-specific details that may be somewhat speculative (e.g., exact upper-left ICM location, extruded cellular bodies/manipulation context), so not fully precise.

Integrates most relevant factors well, including age, BMI, ovarian response, sperm, endometrium, and cycle history, and relates them to prognosis. Minor overinterpretation of stress/alcohol effects and limited handling of the nonspecific diagnosis prevent a top score.

Overall logic is clear and internally consistent, with a plausible probability range tied to embryo grade and patient factors. Some quantitative adjustments are somewhat arbitrary and a few claims (e.g., ICM as strongest predictor, exact decrement from lifestyle factors) are stronger than the evidence supports.

Mostly aligned on embryo grading, transfer appropriateness, avoiding bed rest, and lifestyle optimization. However, recommending PGT-A, freeze-all, ERA after a single failure, acupuncture, and higher progesterone dosing based mainly on BMI goes beyond or weakly aligns with standard guideline-based practice.

Provides clear next-step recommendations for transfer and future planning, including lifestyle changes and follow-up testing. Some suggestions are useful but not sufficiently individualized or evidence-prioritized, so not maximally actionable.
